defects.english: صحيح مسلم — حديث ٢٦٢٦
defects.why: The hadith citation is left in Arabic script instead of being translated or transliterated.
defects.suggestion: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith «لا تحقرن من المعروف شيئا ولو أن تلقى أخاك بوجه طلق» (Sahih Muslim — hadith 2626)

defects.english: صحيح مسلم — حديث ٢٥٩٤
defects.why: The hadith citation is left in Arabic script instead of being translated or transliterated.
defects.suggestion: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith on gentleness (Sahih Muslim — hadith 2594)

defects.english: صحيح البخاري — حديث ١٢٨٣
defects.why: The hadith citation is left in Arabic script instead of being translated or transliterated.
defects.suggestion: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith on patience (Sahih al-Bukhari — hadith 1283)

defects.english: it tells them they are safe and respected
defects.why: The Arabic says the child feels safe and respected, not merely that they are told this.
defects.suggestion: Set aside ten minutes a day to listen to your child without interrupting — it makes them feel safe and respected.

defects.english: praise that names the effort
defects.why: The English narrows the general term 'constructive praise' to one specific technique.
defects.suggestion: Mark the smallest achievement with a kind word: constructive praise builds a confident child who loves doing good.

defects.english: Read your child
defects.why: The Arabic says to read with the child, but the English can be read as reading to them, losing the shared activity.
defects.suggestion: Read with your child the story of a prophet or a companion each night before sleep: the heart grows through example.

defects.english: a visible invitation to settle
defects.why: Arabic 'حافز' means incentive/motivator and 'السكينة' means tranquility; 'invitation to settle' softens the meaning.
defects.suggestion: Give your child a small corner of the house for reading and quiet — a visible incentive for tranquility.

defects.english: small jar
defects.why: Arabic specifies a money box (حصالة), while 'jar' loses the saving/money-box meaning.
defects.suggestion: Keep a small money box at home called “the good money box”, where your child puts whatever they like for those in need.

defects.english: to anything that makes them uncomfortable
defects.why: Arabic limits this to any behaviour (تصرف), while 'anything' broadens it to objects and situations.
defects.suggestion: Teach your child how to say “no” to a stranger, or to any behaviour that makes them uncomfortable.

defects.arabic: علم ابنك أن الاستئذان قبل دخول الغرف أدب قرآني يحمي الخصوصية.
defects.english: Teach your child that asking permission before entering a room is an adab the Qur'an taught, and it protects everyone's privacy.
defects.why: The Arabic uses the plural 'الغرف' and does not say 'everyone's', so the English slightly narrows and expands the original.
defects.suggestion: Teach your child that asking permission before entering rooms is a Qur'anic adab that protects privacy.

defects.arabic: درب طفلك على حفظ سر البيت وعدم نقل التفاصيل الداخلية للخارج.
defects.english: Train your child to keep the household's business inside the house.
defects.why: The English drops the explicit ideas of 'secret' and 'internal details' found in the Arabic.
defects.suggestion: Train your child to keep the household's secrets and not pass on internal details to outsiders.

defects.arabic: اشكر زوجتك أمام الأبناء واشكري زوجك أمامهم: القدوة في احترام الزوجين تنعكس على سلوك الأبناء.
defects.english: Thank your wife in front of the children, and thank your husband in front of them: how the two of you treat each other is what they copy.
defects.why: The English loses the Arabic emphasis on 'example' and 'respect' between spouses.
defects.suggestion: Thank your wife in front of the children, and thank your husband in front of them: the example of respect between spouses is reflected in the children's behaviour.

defects.arabic: عند السفر أو النزهة، اشرك الأطفال في التخطيط واختيار الأنشطة.
defects.english: When you travel or go out, bring the children into the planning and let them choose some of it.
defects.why: The English 'choose some of it' is vague and does not clearly convey 'choosing the activities'.
defects.suggestion: When you travel or go out, bring the children into the planning and choosing the activities.

defects.arabic: «لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين»
defects.english: «لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ»
defects.why: The Quranic ayah should be enclosed in ﴿﴾, not «», in the English rendering.
defects.suggestion: Use ﴿لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾.

defects.arabic: علم طفلك استغفار ودعاء يونس عند الضيق: «لا إله إلا أنت سبحانك إني كنت من الظالمين».
defects.english: Teach your child istighfar and the du'a of Yunus in distress: «...» (al-Anbiya' 21:87 — interpretation of the meaning, Saheeh International: ...)
defects.why: The English adds a Quranic citation and Saheeh International translation not present in the Arabic.
defects.suggestion: Remove the added citation and translation, or keep only the Arabic ayah with ﴿﴾.

defects.english: the character her faith gives her
defects.why: The English drops 'noble' and 'Islamic' from the description of her character.
defects.suggestion: Teach your daughter modesty, and pride in her identity and her noble Islamic character.

defects.english: a rule
defects.why: The English omits 'تربوي' (educational/parenting), making the rule generic.
defects.suggestion: Explain the reason behind an educational decision simply, instead of handing down a bare order.

defects.english: illustrated
defects.why: The English omits 'الممتعة' (enjoyable/interesting).
defects.suggestion: Keep a small library at home with illustrated and enjoyable stories of the prophets.

defects.english: a small, daily sense of responsibility
defects.why: The English adds 'small, daily' and drops the verb 'develop', slightly altering the phrase.
defects.suggestion: Train your child to switch off lights and devices nobody is using to develop a sense of responsibility.

defects.arabic: مراقبة الله عند استخدام النت والموبايل
defects.english: knowing Allah sees them on the internet and on the phone as everywhere else
defects.why: The English adds "as everywhere else", which is not in the Arabic.
defects.suggestion: Teach your child that digital honesty is knowing Allah sees them when they use the internet and phone.

defects.english: their cousins on both sides
defects.why: The Arabic mentions paternal cousins and maternal uncles, while the English says cousins on both sides, changing the relatives.
defects.suggestion: Teach your children to visit their paternal cousins and maternal uncles to strengthen the ties of kinship.

defects.english: help choose and wrap the Eid gifts, and spread the joy with you
defects.why: The English adds "choose" and "with you", which are not in the Arabic; "ترتيب" means arranging.
defects.suggestion: Let your children help arrange and wrap the Eid gifts to spread joy.

defects.arabic: جمال الروح والأخلاق يبصم في قلوب الناس
defects.english: a beautiful character leaves a deeper mark on people
defects.why: The English omits "soul" and "hearts" from the Arabic.
defects.suggestion: Teach your child that beauty of soul and character leaves a deeper mark on people's hearts than expensive clothes ever do.

defects.english: (صحيح مسلم — حديث ٢٦٢٦)
defects.why: Arabic citation text left untranslated in the English field; other items in this set render it in English.
defects.suggestion: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith «لا تحقرن من المعروف شيئا ولو أن تلقى أخاك بوجه طلق» (Sahih Muslim — hadith 2626)

defects.english: (صحيح مسلم — حديث ٢٥٩٤)
defects.why: Arabic citation text left untranslated in the English field.
defects.suggestion: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith on gentleness (Sahih Muslim — hadith 2594)

defects.arabic: الثناء البناء يُنشئ طفلاً واثقاً محباً للخير
defects.english: praise that names the effort builds a confident child who loves doing good
defects.why: The Arabic says 'constructive praise'; the English adds the specific technique 'that names the effort', which is not in the source.
defects.suggestion: Mark the smallest achievement with a kind word: constructive praise builds a confident child who loves doing good.

defects.english: (صحيح البخاري — حديث ١٢٨٣)
defects.why: Arabic citation text left untranslated in the English field.
defects.suggestion: Parenting guidance — drawn from the hadith on patience (Sahih al-Bukhari — hadith 1283)

defects.arabic: اقرأ مع طفلك قصة نبي أو صحابي
defects.english: Read your child the story of a prophet or a companion
defects.why: The Arabic says 'read with your child' (together), but the English reads as 'read to your child' (parent-to-child).
defects.suggestion: Read with your child the story of a prophet or a companion each night before sleep: the heart grows through example.

defects.english: “thank you” and “جزاك الله خيرًا”
defects.why: The Arabic phrase «جزاك الله خيراً» is left in Arabic script in the English field instead of being transliterated or translated.
defects.suggestion: Get your children used to saying “thank you” and “Jazak Allah khayran” for any help around the house.

defects.english: Take your child to the mosque
defects.why: «ابنك» means specifically 'your son'; the English generalises to 'your child'.
defects.suggestion: Take your son to the mosque gently and cheerfully, and teach him stillness through love rather than fear.

defects.english: I am here with you
defects.why: The phrase «وبجانبك» ('and by your side') is dropped from the English.
defects.suggestion: Say instead: I am with you and by your side, and when you are calm we will talk.

defects.arabic: درب طفلك على حفظ سر البيت وعدم نقل التفاصيل الداخلية للخارج.
defects.english: Train your child to keep the household's business inside the house.
defects.why: The Arabic has two distinct points — keeping the household's secret and not transferring internal details to outsiders — but the English condenses them into one clause, losing the explicit 'not sharing internal details outside' element.
defects.suggestion: Train your child to keep the household's secrets and not share its internal details with outsiders.

defects.arabic: مستمدة من حديث النظر إلى القلوب (صحيح مسلم — حديث ٢٥٦٤)
defects.english: drawn from the hadith «إن الله لا ينظر إلى صوركم» (صحيح مسلم — حديث ٢٥٦٤)
defects.why: The Arabic refers to the hadith by its descriptive name ('the hadith of looking at hearts') while the English replaces that with the hadith's text, changing the reference style.
defects.suggestion: drawn from the hadith on looking at hearts (Sahih Muslim — hadith 2564)

defects.english: “I can see that this upset you.”
defects.why: The Arabic example phrase says 'I see that you are sad because of this matter' but the English replaces 'sad' with 'upset' and restructures the sentence, shifting the nuance.
defects.suggestion: “I can see that you are sad because of this.”

defects.english: the character her faith gives her
defects.why: The Arabic specifies 'her noble Islamic character' but the English generalises to 'the character her faith gives her', dropping both 'Islamic' and 'noble'.
defects.suggestion: Teach your daughter modesty, and pride in who she is and in her noble Islamic character.

defects.english: the du'a for travelling
defects.why: The Arabic specifies the du'a for riding/mounting (دعاء الركوب), but the English broadens it to 'travelling'.
defects.suggestion: Teach your child the du'a for riding, and to look for barakah in every journey.

defects.english: a rule
defects.why: The Arabic says 'the parenting/educational decision' (القرار التربوي) but the English reduces it to 'a rule', losing the parenting context.
defects.suggestion: Explain the reason behind a parenting decision simply, instead of handing down a bare order.

defects.english: a small, daily sense of responsibility
defects.why: The English adds 'small, daily' which is not present in the Arabic.
defects.suggestion: Train your child to switch off lights and devices nobody is using, to develop a sense of responsibility.

defects.english: without fearing what follows
defects.why: The Arabic specifies fear of punishment (العقاب); the English softens this to the vague 'what follows'.
defects.suggestion: Get your children used to telling the truth and owning a mistake without fear of punishment.

defects.english: it is another go at learning something
defects.why: The Arabic includes both learning and experience/experimentation (والتجربة); the English drops the latter and rephrases loosely.
defects.suggestion: it is a new opportunity for learning and experience.

defects.english: and to remember what they owe them
defects.why: The Arabic says to preserve/acknowledge the teachers' own virtue and favour (فضلهم); the English shifts the focus to what the child owes them.
defects.suggestion: and to remember their teachers' favour.

defects.arabic: شفرة حب أو كلمة سر لطيفة
defects.english: a small signal or a password
defects.why: The affectionate nuance of 'love code' (شفرة حب) and 'nice/cute' (لطيفة) is dropped in the English.
defects.suggestion: Keep a love code or a cute secret word between you and your children — a quick, private way to reach each other.

defects.english: compete in doing good
defects.why: The qualifier «الشريف» (honourable/fair) is dropped from the English.
defects.suggestion: Teach your children to compete honourably in doing good, without bitterness or envy.

defects.arabic: هي مراقبة الله عند استخدام النت والموبايل
defects.english: knowing Allah sees them on the internet and on the phone as everywhere else
defects.why: The phrase "as everywhere else" is added; the Arabic only mentions internet and phone.
defects.suggestion: Teach your child that digital honesty is knowing Allah sees them when using the internet and the phone.

defects.english: choose and wrap the Eid gifts
defects.why: «ترتيب» means arranging/preparing, not choosing; the English changes the activity.
defects.suggestion: Let your children help arrange and wrap the Eid gifts, and spread the joy.

defects.arabic: جمال الروح والأخلاق يبصم في قلوب الناس
defects.english: a beautiful character leaves a deeper mark on people
defects.why: «الروح» (soul) is dropped and «في قلوب الناس» (in people's hearts) becomes the vaguer "on people".
defects.suggestion: Teach your child that beauty of soul and character leaves a deeper mark in people's hearts than expensive clothes ever do.

defects.english: responsibility learned by doing
defects.why: The English adds the pedagogical claim 'learned by doing' which is not present in the Arabic; the Arabic simply says 'developing a sense of responsibility.'
defects.suggestion: Keep a box at home for recycling paper or saving leftover food — developing a sense of responsibility.

defects.arabic: علم طفلك الاعتزاز بدينه وقيمه وأخلاقه
defects.english: Teach your child to hold to their faith, their values and their character
defects.why: The Arabic 'الاعتزاز' means taking pride in / feeling honored by, but the English 'hold to' means merely adhering to, which understates the intended sense of confident pride.
defects.suggestion: Teach your child to take pride in their faith, their values and their character with confidence and love.
